mainTopic: Unstable סוכות: on a tree, on a ship, on an animal, and using an animal as a wall
overview: The משנה ends its discussion of a סוכה on a tree with a rule: if the סוכה could stand without the tree, it is כשרה. The גמרא says this follows רבי עקיבא, who allows a סוכה on a ship against רבן גמליאל. אביי explains that they argue only about a סוכה that survives a normal land wind but not a stronger one. רבן גמליאל requires a דירת קבע, while רבי עקיבא requires only a דירת עראי. The גמרא then says the משנה's סוכה on a camel follows רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה disqualifies it because a סוכה must be usable all seven days, and רבי מאיר answers that the ban on using an animal on יום טוב is only rabbinic. When an animal is used as a wall, the views flip: רבי מאיר forbids any living thing as a wall. אביי says this is because it might die, and רבי זירא says it is because it might run away. After some back-and-forth, they agree to forbid an untied elephant and disagree only about a tied animal. The amud ends partway through the answer to why אביי still worries about death when the animal is held up by ropes; that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה's general rule for a סוכה on a tree
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states: if the סוכה could stand on its own without the tree, it is כשרה, and one may climb into it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the principle: any case where, if the tree were taken away, the סוכה could still stand by itself, it is fit, and one may go up into it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a summary rule for a סוכה built on or around a tree. The test is whether the סוכה could stand without the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tree is only extra support and not the main support, the סוכה is כשרה. Then going up into it on יום טוב does not count as using a tree, which is forbidden on יום טוב. The tree still sways in the wind, so the סוכה is not perfectly stable. That detail is what the גמרא will pick up next.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will link this rule to the question of how sturdy a סוכה has to be.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
any case where, if the tree were removed,
the sukkah could still stand by itself,
it is fit, and one may go up into it on Yom Tov.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה on a tree is כשרה if it could stand without the tree, and one may enter it on יום טוב.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה? רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the author of the משנה is and answers right away: רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose opinion is our משנה? It is רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by naming whose view the משנה follows. This sets up the next step, where it will bring a source to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה on a tree moves when the wind shakes the tree, so it is not fully stable. The גמרא says only רבי עקיבא would accept such a סוכה. The proof is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara: Whose opinion is our Mishnah?
It is Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose view the משנה in step 1 follows.

steps.title: ברייתא: רבן גמליאל and רבי עקיבא argue about a סוכה on a ship
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבן גמליאל disqualifies a סוכה built on a ship and רבי עקיבא allows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: someone who builds his סוכה on top of a ship — רבן גמליאל rules it invalid, and רבי עקיבא rules it valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי עקיבא allows a shaky סוכה, like one on a ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ship sways and faces strong winds, much like a tree. רבי עקיבא allows a סוכה on a ship, so he would also allow one on a tree, as the משנה does. רבן גמליאל disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught: one who makes his sukkah
on top of the ship —
Rabban Gamliel deems it invalid,
and Rabbi Akiva deems it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 2 that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא validates a סוכה on a ship.

steps.title: The story of the סוכה on the ship
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא built a סוכה on a ship and the wind blew it away. רבן גמליאל asked him, 'Where is your סוכה?'
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident with רבן גמליאל and רבי עקיבא, who were traveling on a ship. רבי עקיבא got up and built a סוכה on top of the ship. The next day a wind blew and uprooted it. רבן גמליאל said to him: עקיבא! Where is your סוכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a story that shows the argument in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's question is a gentle jab. The סוכה could not handle the sea wind, so in his view it was never a real סוכה. The story makes clear that the argument is about a סוכה that cannot survive strong wind.
steps.confusionAlert: The story does not show that רבי עקיבא changed his mind. רבן גמליאל is only showing why he holds his own view. רבי עקיבא's ruling stays the same.

phrases.english: An incident with Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Akiva
who were traveling on a ship.
Rabbi Akiva got up and made a sukkah
on top of the ship.
The next day a wind blew and uprooted it.
Rabban Gamliel said to him:
Akiva! Where is your sukkah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story inside the ברייתא that illustrates the argument from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה on a ship may not survive the sea wind. רבן גמליאל therefore considers it no סוכה at all.

steps.title: אביי: the cases where everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: אביי says both agree on two cases. A סוכה that cannot survive a normal land wind is nothing. A סוכה that can survive even an unusual land wind is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees that where the סוכה cannot stand up to a normal land wind, it is nothing. If it can stand up even to an unusual land wind, everyone agrees that it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins explaining the argument by first setting aside the cases where there is no argument. This prepares for his next point about where they do disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses two kinds of wind: a normal land wind and an unusual (stronger) land wind. Too weak for a normal wind means the סוכה is not even a temporary home. Strong enough for an unusual wind means it is כשרה for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is nothing (not a סוכה at all)

phrases.english: Abaye said: Everyone agrees,
where it cannot stand up
to a normal land wind —
it is nothing.
If it can stand up to an unusual land wind,
everyone agrees that it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the scope of the argument in steps 3 and 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Too weak for a normal land wind means not a סוכה. Strong enough for an unusual land wind means כשרה for all.

steps.title: אביי: the exact case of the disagreement
steps.stepSummary: They argue only about a סוכה that survives a normal land wind but not an unusual land wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is a סוכה that can stand up to a normal land wind but cannot stand up to an unusual land wind.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pinpoints the middle case where the argument happens. This sets up the reasons for each side, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle case is a סוכה that is sturdy enough for normal days on land but fails in stronger winds. A normal sea wind is as strong as an unusual land wind, so a סוכה on a ship falls right into this middle case.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Normal sea wind' and 'unusual land wind' are the same strength. The ship case is simply this middle case.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is where it can stand up
to a normal land wind
but cannot stand up
to an unusual land wind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the cases where both agree, names the case where they disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is limited to a סוכה that survives normal land wind but not unusual land wind (normal sea wind).

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's reason: a סוכה must be a permanent home
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds a סוכה must be a דירת קבע. If it cannot survive a normal sea wind, it is nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל holds: we require a סוכה to be a permanent dwelling, and since it cannot stand up to a normal sea wind, it is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why רבן גמליאל disqualifies the middle case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן גמליאל, a סוכה has to be sturdy like a real, lasting home. A home must survive the normal wind of its own location. On the sea, the normal wind is strong, so a סוכה that fails there does not count.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel holds:
a sukkah must be a permanent dwelling,
and since it cannot stand up
to a normal sea wind —
it is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבן גמליאל's reasoning for the middle case from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה must be a דירת קבע. One that cannot survive the normal sea wind is פסולה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's reason: a temporary home is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds a סוכה only needs to be a דירת עראי. If it survives a normal land wind, it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds: we require a סוכה to be only a temporary dwelling, and since it can stand up to a normal land wind, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes by explaining why רבי עקיבא allows the middle case. This also explains why our משנה allows a סוכה on a tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, a סוכה is meant to be a temporary hut. It only needs the basic sturdiness of handling a normal land wind. A סוכה on a ship or on a swaying tree passes that test, so the משנה matches רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatToRemember: Both agree on the extremes. In the middle case (survives a normal land wind but not a normal sea wind), רבן גמליאל requires a דירת קבע and says פסול, while רבי עקיבא requires only a דירת עראי and says כשר. Our משנה about the tree follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of דירת קבע versus דירת עראי is a basic idea about what a סוכה is, and it comes up in other places in the מסכת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
a sukkah needs only to be a temporary dwelling,
and since it can stand up
to a normal land wind —
it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the argument, opposite רבן גמליאל's view in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא requires only a דירת עראי, so a סוכה that survives a normal land wind is כשרה even on a ship or tree. This is why the משנה follows him.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the camel case in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a סוכה on a camel and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Or on top of a camel, etc.' Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, the סוכה built on a camel, which is כשרה. It is setting up the next move by asking whose opinion this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated without any argument that a סוכה on a camel is כשרה. The גמרא suspects this ruling is not accepted by everyone, so it wants to know which תנא stands behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (Whose opinion is this?)

phrases.english: Or on top of a camel, etc.
Our Mishnah, whose opinion is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ship discussion and moves to the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a סוכה on a camel is כשרה?

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר, as shown by a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי מאיר. A ברייתא records that רבי מאיר allows a סוכה on an animal and רבי יהודה forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר. As a ברייתא teaches: if someone builds his סוכה on top of an animal, רבי מאיר says it is כשרה and רבי יהודה says it is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר. It brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about exactly this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי מאיר is the one who allows a סוכה on an animal, the unsigned משנה that allows it must follow him. This tells us that רבי יהודה disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir.
As it was taught in a baraita:
One who makes his sukka on top of an animal:
Rabbi Meir deems it valid,
and Rabbi Yehuda deems it invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who allows a סוכה on an animal, against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה invalidate a סוכה on an animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה says a סוכה on an animal is פסולה. This sets up the next step, where his source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוכה itself has proper walls and סכך, so at first it is not clear what could be wrong with it. The גמרא wants to know what problem רבי יהודה sees.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic behind רבי יהודה's פסול.

steps.title: A סוכה must be usable for all seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from the פסוק 'seven days' that a סוכה must be fit for use all seven days. A סוכה on an animal cannot be used on שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'You shall make the festival of סוכות for yourself for seven days.' A סוכה that can be used for seven days is called a סוכה. A סוכה that cannot be used for seven days is not called a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's source. The words 'seven days' teach that a real סוכה must be usable for the whole חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים forbade using an animal, including climbing on it, on שבת and יום טוב. So a סוכה on an animal cannot be used on the first day of the חג. Since it is not usable for all seven days, רבי יהודה says it does not count as a סוכה at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a rule: a סוכה has to be fit for the whole חג. The next step asks how רבי מאיר gets around it.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"You shall make for yourself the festival of Sukkot
for seven days."
A sukka that is fit for seven days
is called a sukka.
A sukka that is not fit for seven days
is not called a sukka.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סוכה must be usable all seven days. A סוכה on an animal cannot be used on שבת or יום טוב, so it is פסולה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: by Torah law it is usable
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר agrees with the seven-day rule. He holds that the ban on using an animal on יום טוב is only דרבנן, so by Torah law the סוכה is still fit for seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? This סוכה is also fit by Torah law. It is only the חכמים who made a decree against it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי מאיר answers רבי יהודה's reasoning. By Torah law, the סוכה on the animal can be used all seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on climbing an animal on יום טוב is only a rabbinic decree. A rabbinic ban on using it does not take away its Torah status as a סוכה that is fit for seven days, so רבי מאיר rules it כשרה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר does not reject the seven-day rule. He agrees with it. He only says the problem is rabbinic, so it does not make the סוכה פסולה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir? This too
by Torah law is indeed fit,
and it is the Rabbis who decreed against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי מאיר against רבי יהודה's seven-day reasoning.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that a סוכה on an animal is כשרה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing Torah law from a rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the סוכה cannot be used on יום טוב, it fails the seven-day rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is usable by Torah law. A rabbinic ban does not take away its status as a סוכה.

steps.title: Using an animal as a wall: the opinions flip
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if an animal is used as a wall of a סוכה, רבי מאיר says פסול and רבי יהודה says כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made the animal into a wall for the סוכה, רבי מאיר says it is פסולה and רבי יהודה says it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second case, where a living animal is used as one of the walls. Here the two opinions reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the two cases depend on different issues. Standing on an animal is about the seven-day rule. Being made of an animal is about whether a living thing can count as a wall.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. On the animal, רבי מאיר is lenient. As the wall, רבי מאיר is strict.

phrases.english: If he made the animal a wall for the sukka,
Rabbi Meir deems it invalid
and Rabbi Yehuda deems it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new case: the animal as a wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal used as a סוכה wall: רבי מאיר says פסול, רבי יהודה says כשר.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's rule: no living thing as a halachic wall or object
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that anything alive cannot be a סוכה wall, a לחי for an alleyway, a פס around wells, or a גולל for a grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to say: anything that has a living spirit cannot be used as a wall for a סוכה, a side post for an alleyway, boards around wells, or a covering stone for a grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains רבי מאיר's view with a general rule. A living creature cannot serve as any of these halachic structures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule reaches beyond סוכה. It covers עירוב-type structures for שבת (לחי, פסין) and טומאה structures (גולל). Whatever the reason is, it applies to all living things in all these areas.

keyTerms.meaning: Side post that lets one carry in an alleyway on שבת
Upright boards around wells (for carrying on שבת)

phrases.english: For Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רוּחַ חַיִּים,
phrases.english: Anything that has a living spirit,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין עוֹשִׂין אוֹתוֹ לֹא דּוֹפֶן לְסוּכָּה,
phrases.english: one may not make it a wall for a sukka,
nor a side post for an alleyway,
nor boards for wells,
nor a covering for a grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the general principle behind רבי מאיר's ruling in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A living thing cannot serve as a סוכה wall, לחי, פסין, or גולל.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי adds: no גיטין written on an animal
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יוסי הגלילי's name, the list is extended: a גט may not be written on a living animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי they said: one also may not write divorce documents on it.
steps.whatsHappening: A further item is added to רבי מאיר's list. A גט cannot be written on a living creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes the 'no living things' idea beyond walls and structures into documents. The text here does not give a reason for this addition; it simply adds גיטין to the list of things a living creature cannot be used for.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili they said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵין כּוֹתְבִין עָלָיו גִּיטֵּי נָשִׁים.
phrases.english: Also, one may not write bills of divorce on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט may not be written on a living animal.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר reject a living wall?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the concern is behind רבי מאיר's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a living animal cannot be a wall. This sets up two answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal is physically solid and tall enough, so the problem is not obvious. The גמרא is looking for the hidden worry.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind the rule in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What concern makes a living thing unfit as a wall?

steps.title: אביי: it might die; רבי זירא: it might run away
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the worry is that the animal might die. רבי זירא says the worry is that it might run away.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: maybe it will die. רבי זירא said: maybe it will run away.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different worries about using a living animal as a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי worries the animal will die, fall down, and no longer be a standing wall. רבי זירא worries the animal will walk away and leave the סוכה without a wall. Both views mean the wall is not reliable.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Lest it die.
Rabbi Zeira said: Lest it flee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 with two explanations.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי: the concern is death. רבי זירא: the concern is fleeing.

steps.title: A tied elephant: everyone agrees it is fine
steps.stepSummary: With a tied elephant, both views agree it works as a wall. It cannot flee, and even if it dies, its body is still ten טפחים tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a tied elephant, everyone agrees. Even if it dies, its carcass is still ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to show how אביי and רבי זירא differ in practice. It begins with a case where they agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tied elephant cannot run away, which answers רבי זירא's worry. Its dead body is still at least ten טפחים tall, the minimum height for a wall, which answers אביי's worry. So both sides allow it.

phrases.english: With a tied elephant,
everyone agrees,
for even if it dies,
its carcass has a height of ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפִיל קָשׁוּר כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts defining the practical difference between the two reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tied elephant is a valid wall according to both reasons.

steps.title: An untied elephant: here they disagree
steps.stepSummary: With an untied elephant, אביי has no concern, since even its carcass is tall enough. רבי זירא is still concerned that it may run away.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about an elephant that is not tied. According to the one who says 'maybe it will die,' we are not worried. According to the one who says it is a decree because 'maybe it will run away,' we are worried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pinpoints the practical difference between אביי and רבי זירא: an untied elephant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is death, an elephant is fine even untied, because its body still stands ten טפחים. If the worry is running away, an untied elephant can walk off, so it remains פסול.
steps.whatToRemember: A living animal cannot be a סוכה wall according to רבי מאיר. אביי says it is because it may die, and רבי זירא says it is because it may run away. This first proposal (they disagree about an untied elephant) is challenged and replaced in steps 21–22.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is an elephant that is not tied.
According to the one who said 'lest it die,'
we are not concerned.
According to the one who said it is a decree 'lest it flee,'
we are concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the practical-difference analysis begun in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: First proposal: the practical difference between אביי and רבי זירא is an untied elephant (כשר according to אביי, פסול according to רבי זירא). Step 22 rejects this.

steps.title: Why would אביי not also worry that the animal flees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that אביי has no concern with an untied elephant. Fleeing is a real worry for him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the decree is out of fear that the animal will die, let him also be concerned that it will run away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous conclusion (Step 20). It had said אביי is not bothered by an untied elephant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי worries about death, but nothing in his reasoning rules out a second worry about fleeing. An untied elephant can obviously walk away. So it makes no sense to say אביי would allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us be concerned / we should worry
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

phrases.english: According to the one who said it is a decree lest it die,
let him be concerned lest it flee!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת, נֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא תִּבְרַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 20's claim that אביי permits an untied elephant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 20 that אביי has no concern with an untied elephant.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fleeing is a reasonable concern for anyone, so אביי should worry about it too.

steps.title: The dispute is really about a tied animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses its earlier explanation. Everyone forbids an untied elephant. The disagreement is only about an ordinary animal that is tied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: with an elephant that is not tied, everyone agrees it is not valid. They disagree about a tied ordinary animal. The one who worries about death is concerned, because an ordinary dead animal is less than ten טפחים tall. The one who worries about fleeing is not concerned, because a tied animal cannot flee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and rebuilds the explanation of the dispute from scratch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an untied elephant, fleeing is a risk, so both אביי and רבי זירא forbid it. With a tied ordinary animal, fleeing is impossible but death is still possible. A dead ordinary animal is under ten טפחים. So אביי forbids it and רבי זירא permits it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 20. That explanation said they disagree about an untied elephant. It is now replaced. They agree about the untied elephant and disagree about a tied ordinary animal.

phrases.english: Rather:
with an elephant that is not tied,
everyone agrees (it is invalid).
Where they disagree is about a tied animal.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת — חָיְישִׁינַן.
phrases.english: According to the one who says it is a decree lest it die, we are concerned.
phrases.notes: That's because an ordinary animal, once it's dead, is less than ten טפחים tall.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא תִּבְרַח — לָא חָיְישִׁינַן.
phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is a decree lest it flee, we are not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בְּפִיל שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָשׁוּר, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by moving the dispute to a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They disagree about an untied elephant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both forbid an untied elephant. They disagree only about a tied ordinary animal.
steps.whatToRemember: Untied elephant: both forbid it, because it may flee. Tied ordinary animal: אביי forbids it, because it may die; רבי זירא permits it.

steps.title: Why would רבי זירא not worry about death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the opposite question: why does רבי זירא ignore the possibility that the tied animal dies?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says the decree is lest it flee: let him be concerned lest it die?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same type of challenge back on רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 has רבי זירא permitting a tied animal. A tied animal can still die and shrink below ten טפחים. So why is he not worried?

phrases.english: And the one who says it is a decree lest it flee,
let him be concerned lest it die?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא תִּבְרַח, נֵיחוּשׁ שֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's side of the new explanation in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא permitting a tied animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Death is also a possible risk, so he should worry about it too.

steps.title: Death is not common
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא does not worry about death because a healthy animal suddenly dying is unusual.
steps.simpleTranslation: Death is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 23 with a short, simple reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים do not make a גזרה for rare situations. For רבי זירא, an animal dying during the חג is rare enough to ignore. Running away is common, so it does need a safeguard.

phrases.english: Death is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Probability: rare cases do not get a גזרה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא should worry about death as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Death is rare, so he does not make a גזרה for it.

steps.title: What about the gap between the legs?
steps.stepSummary: The space under and between the animal's legs is like a big hole in the wall. How can this count as a wall?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the open space in between the legs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a practical problem that applies to both opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall whose open part is larger than its solid part is not valid. The area between an animal's legs is mostly empty. So the animal may not count as a wall at all.

phrases.english: But isn't there the open space in between (the legs)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the dispute to a practical problem with the case itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using an animal as a wall at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The gaps between the legs make the open part larger than the solid part.

steps.title: Filling the gaps with palm and laurel leaves
steps.stepSummary: The person fills in the gaps with branches, so the wall is solid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He fills it in with palm leaves and laurel branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 25 by describing how the case actually works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gaps are stuffed with plant material. Now the animal plus the leaves forms a complete wall. The animal's height is still what provides the ten טפחים.

phrases.english: He makes it (closed) with palm leaves and laurel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gaps make the wall invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gaps are filled in, so the wall is complete.

steps.title: What if the animal crouches?
steps.stepSummary: Even if it will not die, the animal might lie down and become shorter than ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And perhaps it will crouch down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another practical worry about a tied animal, especially for רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying down is far more common than dying. If the animal crouches, the wall drops below ten טפחים. So even רבי זירא should have a concern here.

phrases.english: And perhaps it will crouch?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new practical challenge to permitting a tied animal.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא permitting a tied animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Crouching is common and would make the wall too short.

steps.title: The animal is held up by ropes from above
steps.stepSummary: The animal is tied with ropes from above, so it cannot lie down.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is stretched up with ropes from above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 27 by adding a detail to the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is tied both to stop it from fleeing and with ropes from above. The ropes hold it upright, so crouching is impossible.

phrases.english: It is held taut with ropes from above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ropes from above keep it upright.

steps.title: Then אביי should not worry about death either
steps.stepSummary: If ropes hold the animal up, its body would stay standing even if it died. So why is אביי concerned?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says the decree is lest it die, also: it is held up with ropes from above!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the answer of Step 28 to challenge אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same ropes that stop crouching would also keep a dead body upright at full height. So the worry about death seems to disappear. That would leave no reason for אביי to forbid a tied animal.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת נָמֵי,
phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is a decree lest it die, also,
but it is held taut with ropes from above!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא תָּמוּת נָמֵי, הָא מְתִיחָה בְּאַשְׁלֵי מִלְּעֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of Step 28 into a challenge against אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's concern about death with a tied animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ropes from above would keep even a dead body standing tall.

steps.title: Sometimes the animal is placed just below the סכך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer. Sometimes the animal is not ten טפחים tall by itself. It stands within three טפחים of the סכך and counts as reaching it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he sets it up less than three טפחים from the סכך…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer Step 29. This is a setup line, and the rest of the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a short animal that stands within three טפחים of the סכך. It counts as a complete wall through לבוד, the rule that a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed. In this setup even a slight shrinking at death could open a gap of three טפחים. The next lines will spell this out.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not finished here. The animal is shorter than ten טפחים and counts as a full wall only because the gap above it to the סכך is under three טפחים (לבוד). The explanation of why death matters in this setup continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Sometimes he positions it
less than three (טפחים) close to the roofing,

steps.triggerLanguage: זִמְנִין דְּמוֹקֵים בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה סָמוּךְ לַסְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing (the answer continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ropes from above remove any concern about death.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some setups depend on the animal staying within three טפחים of the סכך, so death can still cause a problem.
